The platform offers a wider selection and additional incentives for customers. Lucknow and Ahmedabad are leading markets for these premium rakhi purchases. Customers are increasingly starting their Rakhi shopping several days ahead of the festival.

items.title: Mission vs profit at Anthropic: AI company's interview questions try to judge candidates’ ethical stance, says report
items.summary: Anthropic emphasises mission-driven values on its careers page, highlighting a tension between mission and profit. The company has made principled decisions regarding contracts and hiring practices .

items.summary: India has attracted inflows of $73 billion in 11 weeks, driven mostly by foreign currency bank deposits made by non-resident Indians.

items.summary: Kyiv says the attacks are aimed at disrupting Russian supply chains and inflicting further pressure on Putin's wartime economy.

items.title: Avaada Group plans Rs 10,000 crore green industrial campus in Haryana’s Hisar
items.summary: Avaada Group plans to invest around ₹10,000 crore to develop a 300-acre green industrial campus in Hisar, Haryana. The Zero-CBAM project, aimed at helping industries meet global carbon requirements, is expected to create more than 5,000 jobs.

items.title: Oil fall lifts rupee to over one-week high after central bank keeps lid on losses
items.summary: The Indian rupee surged to a one-week peak on Tuesday, empowered by the recent dip in oil prices alongside measures taken by the central bank. Throughout the trading day, the rupee remained within a narrow band as Brent crude prices decreased by more than three percent. Concurrently, Asian currencies showed slight declines, with the dollar index slipping beneath 99.

items.title: Global Market: Japanese businesses turn to currency hedging as weak Yen drives up import costs
items.summary: Japanese businesses are increasingly turning to longer-term supplier agreements and currency hedging as the yen’s prolonged weakness raises import costs and makes expenses harder to predict. Companies are locking in prices and exchange rates for longer periods, while exporters are also seeking protection against currency swings as uncertainty over the yen’s outlook persists.

items.title: Sensex rises 287 points, Nifty closes above 24,300 as market swings into green on first monthly expiry after CAS
items.summary: The Indian stock market ended higher on Tuesday after a volatile session, with Sensex gaining 287 points and Nifty rising 115 points. Pharma, PSU banks and consumer durables led sectoral gains, while private banks and metals declined. IndiGo, Adani Ports, Infosys and Trent gained, while Eternal and HCLTech fell.

items.summary: The Indian stock market recovered by close on August 25, buoyed by late buying; Nifty 50 gained 0.17% and Sensex 0.21%. Despite gains, market sentiment stayed fragile amid heightened tensions related to U.S. sanctions on Iran.

items.summary: The site hosts a range of subscription-based content from cooking to fitness videos, but it is best known for pornography.

items.summary: Mutual funds have steadily raised their holdings in several large-cap stocks over the past two quarters, with nine such stocks delivering 25-50% gains in CY26 so far. Data from ACE Equity shows that Adani Energy Solutions, Lenskart Solutions and ABB India led the pack, while Adani Power, Siemens, Bosch, Adani Green Energy, Billionbrains Garage Ventures and Titan Company also recorded strong gains alongside rising MF ownership.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc shares fall 3% on reports of fresh government stake sale via OFS
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc shares dropped on Tuesday after expectations of a fresh government stake sale through an OFS resurfaced following the Hindustan Copper stake sale. The government is reportedly considering selling around 1.5% of Hindustan Zinc, which could raise Rs 3,500-4,000 crore. The stock has declined nearly 3% in 2026.

items.title: How to start taking control of your finances: A practical first step for women
items.summary: Financial independence starts with understanding how money is earned, spent, saved and invested. For women looking to take greater control of their finances, building an emergency fund, setting clear goals and improving financial literacy can provide a practical starting point for making more confident financial decisions.

items.title: Boundless VC closes ₹300 crore fund to back early-stage AI, frontier-tech firms
items.summary: This comes at a time when India has fallen behind the US and China in building globally competitive foundational AI models. While the industry sees greater opportunities for Indian startups at the application layer, a lack of early-stage local risk capital may pose challenges.

items.summary: Ebix shares surged by 5% to ₹22.02, hitting an upper circuit for six consecutive sessions after rebounding 36% from its 52-week low. The company also issued over one crore NCMC RuPay smart cards, and its payments subsidiary received RBI approval to conduct trade remittances.

items.summary: The SEC is seeking information from major Wall Street banks about trades and financing tied to AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness.

items.summary: SoftBank has reduced its stake in Lenskart by offloading shares worth ₹2,888 crore, following a previous sale of ₹2,873 crore. Its holding has fallen from 9.86% to 7.28%, making it the second-largest public shareholder in the eyewear company.

items.title: Global trade shake-up reaches fashion as Zara supplier Pearl Global eyes Africa market
items.summary: Pearl Global eyes North Africa and Jordan for manufacturing expansion. This move aims to serve European customers and diversify production bases. The company is reducing its reliance on the United States market. Other Indian garment exporters are also increasing African production. Pearl Global anticipates significant revenue growth in the coming years.

items.title: India targets $55 trillion economy by2047 through AI, manufacturing, FDI and sunrise sectors
items.summary: India aims for a $55 trillion economy by 2047. This ambitious goal relies on leveraging its young demographic in artificial intelligence. Strategic capital deployment and sustained growth will unlock value across core sectors. Attracting foreign investment and expanding manufacturing are vital for this economic expansion. Dominance in sunrise sectors like space and defense tech will drive this future growth.

items.title: Vishal Mega Mart gets a 5-year vote of confidence
items.summary: Gunender Kapur’s reappointment eases a key investor concern, but promoter stake sales, intensifying competition and a richer valuation could test the stock’s next leg of growth.

items.title: BlackBerry CEO says robotics is one of its fastest-growing businesses
items.summary: BlackBerry CEO John Giamatteo says robotics is one of QNX’s fastest-growing businesses as the company expands its software beyond cars.

items.title: Why did FACT, RCF, NFL and other fertiliser stocks rally up to 14% today? Explained
items.summary: Fertiliser stocks, including FACT and Rashtriya Chemicals, rose up to 13% on August 25 after Russia assured India of uninterrupted energy and fertiliser supplies during Jaishankar's meeting with Putin, signaling deepening economic ties ahead of the BRICS summit.

items.title: Tata Communications, Tata Motors partner to launch 5G-powered Sierra.ev
items.summary: Tata Communications and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles have partnered to equip the Sierra.ev with built-in 5G connectivity, integrating Tata Communications’ MOVE platform with Tata Motors’ N.IO software-defined vehicle architecture. The setup will enable seamless digital experiences, content streaming, faster over-the-air updates, remote diagnostics, and enhanced personalisation for connected mobility.

items.title: Sugar ex-mill prices down 18 pc to Rs 55/kg after import move, curbs on hoarding: Food secretary
items.summary: Ex-mill sugar prices have dropped eighteen percent to fifty-five rupees per kilogram. This decline follows government measures to curb speculation and allow imports. The food secretary stated prices were artificially inflated by mills previously. Wholesale and retail prices have not yet reflected this significant ex-mill reduction. Government actions aim to stabilize sugar costs for consumers nationwide.

items.title: Retailers keep price hikes in check amid rising input costs: Nuvama
items.summary: Indian retailers are limiting price hikes despite volatile cotton, yarn and fabric costs and geopolitical supply-chain risks. Companies are adjusting sourcing, building safety stocks and selectively absorbing costs to protect demand. Value retail and electronics remain strong, while festive demand is expected to support growth after a softer second quarter.

items.title: Vodafone Idea shares surge 7%: Is SBI-led debt deal finally nearing closure?
items.summary: Vodafone Idea shares rose sharply after reports that a consortium of public-sector banks led by SBI is nearing approval of a larger debt package for the telecom operator. The funding is part of Vi’s broader Rs 45,000-crore requirement and could provide financial flexibility to expand its network and execute planned capex.

items.summary: Leveraging the funding boost, the Ministry eyes higher oil and gas production in the Deep and Ultra Deep waters.

items.summary: India's steel industry is likely to see a volume-led recovery in the second half of FY27, supported by lower input costs, easing maintenance disruptions and strong domestic demand, according to Yes Securities Institutional Equities.

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman agree on a $7 bn investment in the anime theme park.

items.summary: Kedaara Capital has acquired a majority stake in Tynor Orthotics for $200 million. This private equity firm is expanding its medical devices portfolio with this significant investment. Tynor Orthotics is a leading Indian manufacturer of orthopaedic and rehabilitation products. The company has a wide distribution network reaching many countries globally. Kedaara will partner with existing promoters and management to drive future growth.

items.title: Strong Returns! IPO market heats up with 25% average listing gains in two months
items.summary: India’s IPO market has staged a strong comeback in July-August, with 18 of 22 listings delivering positive debut-day returns. Average listing gains stood at 25%, sharply above the 7% recorded in Q1FY27. Analysts expect momentum to continue, supported by strong investor sentiment, attractive valuations and major upcoming IPOs.

items.title: Global Market: European markets gain as investors assess impact of Iran sanctions
items.summary: European shares edged higher on Tuesday, as investors took some relief from the lack of immediate penalties following the latest US sanctions warning against Iran. Defence stocks led gains, rising about 1%, while the measured rollout of the measures eased concerns over disruptions to global trade and energy supplies.

items.title: Exports key for mobile brands to maximize Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme incentives: Kotak
items.summary: New mobile phone manufacturing incentives will prioritize export growth for brands. Domestic market growth alone may not meet scheme targets. Exports are seen as the key lever for maximizing incentive payouts. The scheme aims to boost India's global manufacturing competitiveness. It also supports domestic brands in achieving technological sovereignty.

items.summary: India has mobilised about $73 billion in foreign currency in under 11 weeks, largely through FCNR(B) deposits, yet the rupee remains near ₹95-96 per dollar. The inflows are primarily strengthening RBI’s foreign-exchange buffers rather than being used to push the currency higher.

items.title: Japanese bond ETFs attract a record $1.5 billion in net inflows in 2026 so far, Morningstar say
items.summary: This year, Japanese bond exchange traded funds have experienced an unprecedented surge in inflows, driven by increasing government bond yields that enhance the appeal of Japan's debt for investors. European market participants are diversifying their portfolios, moving away from US dollar assets due to growing uncertainties surrounding the dollar's reliability as a safe haven. Consequently, Japanese bonds present an attractive option with solid yields and developed-market risk.

items.summary: India’s data centre footprint is projected to exceed 101 million sq ft and capacity 6.7 GW by 2030, driven by cloud adoption, AI, digital payments and enterprise digitisation. This collaboration aims to enhance charging accessibility and reduce customer anxiety.

items.summary: Tata Steel received interim relief from a Rs 1,755 crore demand by Jharkhand. The Ministry of Coal's Revisional Authority will consider the company's challenge. Authorities are barred from taking coercive action against Tata Steel for now. This order protects the company while its dispute is pending. The underlying demand remains under review by the Revisional Authority.

items.title: You may soon have to pay a lot less for onions in Delhi-NCR; what you need to know ahead of festive season
items.summary: The Centre plans to sell onions at Rs 35 per kg through mobile vans. This intervention aims to provide relief to consumers facing rising prices. Subsidised onions will be available across Delhi-NCR later this week. The government is also transporting onions from Nashik via special trains. Onion availability remains comfortable despite recent retail price increases.

items.summary: In a bold move, FedEx has announced a USD 150 million investment to create a new air cargo hub spanning 2,30,000 square feet at Delhi airport. This hub will enhance connectivity in North and East India and is poised to exponentially raise package processing from 600 to 5,000 packages every hour. Construction is expected to begin soon, reflecting FedEx's commitment to long-term growth in the region.

Stronger German growth reinforced expectations for ECB rate hikes, keeping borrowing costs high across Europe.

India continues to shine as a key player but is not immune to the threats posed by rising oil costs and inflation.

Reuters calculations based on IEA data show that Iran, Russia, Ukraine, Libya and Venezuela produced around 45 million barrels per day in 2025, accounting for more than 43% of global oil supply.

items.title: Wholesale buyers savour softening sugar even as households' wait for a sweeter deal continues

Traders are optimistic about further reductions as fresh supplies are set to arrive shortly. However, consumers will not notice a drop in retail prices just yet as old inventory needs to be sold off first.

items.title: 'India is a country ripe for innovation across many facets of our business': Marriott International CEO
items.summary: Marriott sees India as a key growth market, planning significant expansion and new hotel openings. The company is adapting its brands and products to suit Indian consumer preferences. Innovation is a focus, with India serving as a testing ground for new initiatives. Artificial intelligence is being integrated into operations to enhance efficiency and guest experiences. Marriott remains committed to long-term growth and adapting to evolving travel trends globally.
